card.stem: The external wall of a house built in the 1970s is constructed using a single leaf 215 mm hollow concrete block. The wall is rendered externally and plasterboard is fixed to the internal surface using dabs of plaster adhesive, as shown in the accompanying sketch.
card.questionText: Calculate the U-value of the external hollow block wall, given the following data: External render thickness 15 mm; Concrete hollow block thickness 215 mm; Air space between plasterboard and block width 10 mm; Internal plasterboard thickness 12 mm. Thermal data of external wall of house: Resistance of external surface (R) 0.048 m2 °C/W; Resistivity of external render (r) 2.170 m °C/W; Resistance of hollow block (R) 0.210 m2 °C/W; Resistance of airspace (R) 0.170 m2 °C/W; Conductivity of plasterboard (k) 0.160 W/m °C; Resistance of internal surface (R) 0.104 m2 °C/W.

rows.contextNote: The calculation set out in a table of material, conductivity or resistivity, thickness and resistance.

Six resistances, 3 each: external surface 0.048 (given); render 0.015 × 2.170 = 0.03255; hollow block 0.210 (given); air space 0.170 (given); plasterboard 0.012/0.160 = 0.075; internal surface 0.104 (given). All in m²°C/W.
Total resistance, the sum of R = 0.63955 m²°C/W.

rows.verbatim: U Value (1 mark for the formula)
rows.contextNote: U = 1/Rt = 1 ÷ 0.63955 = 1.563599 W/m²K (1 mark for the formula).

Thermal data of external wall of house: Resistance of external surface (R) 0.048 m2 °C/W; Resistivity of external render (r) 2.170 m °C/W; Resistance of hollow block (R) 0.210 m2 °C/W; Resistance of airspace (R) 0.170 m2 °C/W; Conductivity of plasterboard (k) 0.160 W/m °C; Resistance of internal surface (R) 0.104 m2 °C/W.

(b) It is proposed to upgrade the thermal properties of the wall by fixing expanded polystyrene to the external surface. Given the thermal conductivity (k) of expanded polystyrene as 0.037 W/m °C, calculate the thickness of expanded polystyrene required to achieve a U-value of 0.27 W/m2 °C to meet the requirements of the current Building Regulations.

(c) In the past, many dwelling houses were built using hollow concrete blocks, as outlined at 5 (a) above. Discuss two disadvantages of this type of construction, and using notes and freehand sketches, recommend a preferred external wall type suitable for a contemporary house.

rows.contextNote: The calculation set out in a table of material, conductivity or resistivity, thickness and resistance.

Six resistances, 3 each: external surface 0.048 (given); render 0.015 × 2.170 = 0.03255; hollow block 0.210 (given); air space 0.170 (given); plasterboard 0.012/0.160 = 0.075; internal surface 0.104 (given). All in m²°C/W.
Total resistance, the sum of R = 0.63955 m²°C/W.

rows.verbatim: U Value (1 mark for the formula)
rows.contextNote: U = 1/Rt = 1 ÷ 0.63955 = 1.563599 W/m²K (1 mark for the formula).

rows.verbatim: Resistance for U-value of 0.27 (2 marks for formula R=1/U)
rows.contextNote: R = 1/U = 1 ÷ 0.27 = 3.703 m²K/W (2 marks for the formula).
The existing resistance, 0.63955 m²K/W.

rows.verbatim: Application of Formula R = T/k (1 mark for formula)
rows.contextNote: R = T/k solved for T: T = R × k = 3.06345 × 0.037 (1 mark for the formula).
T = 0.1133476 metres: 113 mm of expanded polystyrene.
Such as: each hollow block and its ribs form thermal bridges; no insulation in the block or the wall, so heat is lost.
A second, different disadvantage. Such as: impractical to fill with insulation retrospectively; a risk of damp penetrating the hollow block.

Such as: a 350 mm cavity wall with 100 mm rigid insulation and ties; hollow block filled with insulation and 300 mm external insulation with acrylic render; 225 mm block on flat with 300 mm external insulation; or timber frame with a block outer leaf.

Windows and Glazing: triple glazing with U below 0.8 W/m²K, low-conductivity spacers, low-e coatings and g ≥ 50; insulated, thermally broken frames; more south and less north glazing, with shading against summer overheating.
